description: Pipeline tool for indie cookbook publishers — a kanban-style workspace where recipe developers, editors, and photographers move recipes from draft to print across multiple cookbook projects

pages.name: board
pages.description: Kanban board view of every recipe in the current cookbook project, organized by production stage
components: Top bar with the imprint name, a cookbook-project switcher dropdown, a global search, and a stacked-avatar group showing collaborators with an 'Invite' button
Sub-header strip with the active cookbook title, target page count, deadline date, a progress bar showing recipes-complete vs total, and view-toggle controls (Board, Table, Calendar)
Filter bar with chips for course (Starters, Mains, Sides, Desserts, Drinks), an assignee selector, a 'Needs photo' toggle, and a 'Has allergens flagged' toggle

Five-column kanban board (Drafting, Testing, Editing, Photographed, Print-ready) — each column has a heading with recipe count, an 'Add recipe' button, and a stack of recipe cards (title, course, assignee, yield, thumbnail)

pages.name: recipe
pages.description: Detail view of a single recipe card opened from the board, with the full working document
components: Breadcrumb row (Cookbook / Course / Recipe name) with a stage-pill showing current kanban column and a 'Move to next stage' button
Header block with recipe title, headnote paragraph, byline of the developer, yield/servings stepper, total time, and a metadata row for oven temp, equipment, and dietary tags
Two-column working area — left has an ingredient list grouped by sub-recipe (weight, volume, ingredient, prep note), right has numbered method steps with editor notes pinned to specific steps
Test-kitchen log panel listing each test attempt — date, tester name, batch number, outcome rating, and a notes paragraph, with an 'Add test' button at the bottom
Right rail with allergen checklist, cost-per-serving calculation, cross-references to related recipes in the book, and a photo-brief block showing shot list and styling notes

pages.name: calendar
pages.description: Production calendar showing test-kitchen days, photo shoots, and editorial deadlines
components: Top bar (same as board) with a month-navigation control and a 'Today' button on the right
Legend row mapping color swatches to event types (Test day, Photo shoot, Copyedit due, Print deadline) with a per-cookbook filter dropdown
Month grid with seven columns — each day cell shows the date and a stack of event chips with title and time, and weekend cells render on a distinct surface

Side panel listing the selected day's events in detail — each event shows time range, attached recipe titles, assigned crew, location (Studio A, Studio B, Home kitchen), and an 'Add to my schedule' button

pages.name: pantry
pages.description: Master ingredient library shared across all cookbook projects, used for consistency and sourcing
components: Top bar (same as board) with a 'New ingredient' primary button on the right
Two-pane layout — left pane is a category tree (Produce, Dairy, Grains, Spices, Fats, Proteins, Pantry, Ferments) with expand/collapse and counts per category

Right pane is a table of ingredients with columns for name, preferred supplier, unit cost, seasonality strip (twelve month-cells shaded by availability), allergen flags, and a 'used in N recipes' link
Footer drawer with a sourcing-notes editor for the selected ingredient — supplier contacts, substitution rules, and a changelog of price updates

pages.name: imprint
pages.description: Public-facing catalog page for the indie publisher showing their cookbook projects in progress and released
components: Masthead with the imprint name, a one-line manifesto, and a navigation row (Catalog, Authors, Stockists, Submissions)
Featured cookbook block with cover mockup, title, author byline, release date, page count, and a 'Pre-order' button alongside a 'Read sample recipe' link
Catalog grid (three per row) — each cookbook tile shows cover, title, author, status badge (In development, Forthcoming, In print), and a brief description
Submissions block with a heading 'Pitch us a cookbook', a numbered list of three submission steps, and a 'Read the guidelines' link
